stops.date_confidence: attested for the public solution of the headstone cipher by Elonka Dunin on 17 April 2017 (Wikipedia, 'William F. Friedman', citing Dunin's dated solution note). The same year saw Jason Fagone's 'The Woman Who Smashed Codes' (Time, 2017). The Baconian claim that the stone secretly reads 'FRANCIS BACON IS SHAKESPEARE' is tradition circulated by the Francis Bacon Society and is not established; it is marked as a claim in the campa, not as fact.
notes: hard triggers (not established, traditional) discounted: the day is explicitly attested and their clause names no date, year, month or number (it concerns the pin, the house or the sources)

stops.stop: Pascagoula, Mississippi: the hull that was never launched
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'USCGC Friedman'): naming announced 21 December 2018, not July 2020 as the pool's afterlife lens had it; hull WMSL-760; fabrication begun 11 May 2021 at Huntington Ingalls Industries, Pascagoula; contract cancelled 5 June 2025 by agreement between the shipbuilder and the administration; never completed, never launched, never commissioned. The pool attributed the ship to a Smithsonian article that does not mention it; reattributed here.
